topic.title: Proteomic Signatures of Baricitinib Response in Severe Alopecia Areata
topic.abstract: Background: Alopecia areata (AA) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by non-scarring hair loss. Although baricitinib is effective in severe AA, biomarkers associated with subsequent treatment response remain unclear. Methods: In this retrospective real-world study, 110 Chinese patients with severe AA received baricitinib for up to 36 weeks. Baseline plasma samples from 51 patients with AA and 22 healthy controls underwent proteomic profiling. Proteins associated with Week 24 achievement of SALT20 (absolute SALT score ≤ 20) or SALT50 (≥ 50% reduction from baseline) were evaluated alongside clinical variables in multivariable analyses. Selected candidate biomarkers were further evaluated by ELISA. Paired baseline and Week 24 samples were analyzed in 19 patients. Results: At Week 24, 38.2% of patients achieved SALT20 and 54.5% achieved SALT50; by Week 36, these rates increased to 49.3% and 60.3%, respectively. Week 24 achievement of SALT20 or SALT50 was associated with shorter disease duration, lower baseline SALT score, and lower frequencies of AU/AT and eyebrow/eyelash involvement. Compared with healthy controls, patients with AA showed distinct baseline plasma proteomic alterations. Achievers showed a relatively higher baseline inflammatory plasma proteomic profile, and exploratory longitudinal analyses revealed broader post-treatment reductions in inflammatory proteins. CCL11 was higher at baseline in patients who subsequently achieved SALT20 or SALT50 and remained associated with both endpoints in multivariable analysis. Conclusions: Baricitinib response was heterogeneous in patients with severe AA. Better outcomes were associated with higher baseline levels of several inflammatory plasma proteins. CCL11 emerged as a candidate response-associated biomarker.

[상세 내용] (초록 4개 항목 정리 — 이 논문은 전문이 아직 공개되지 않아 초록을 씁니다)

◆ 배경 — Background
  · Alopecia areata (AA) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by non-scarring hair loss.
  · Although baricitinib is effective in severe AA, biomarkers associated with subsequent treatment response remain unclear.

◆ 연구 방법 — Methods
  · In this retrospective real-world study, 110 Chinese patients with severe AA received baricitinib for up to 36 weeks.
  · Baseline plasma samples from 51 patients with AA and 22 healthy controls underwent proteomic profiling.
  · Proteins associated with Week 24 achievement of SALT20 (absolute SALT score ≤ 20) or SALT50 (≥ 50% reduction from baseline) were evaluated alongside clinical variables in multivariable analyses.
  · Selected candidate biomarkers were further evaluated by ELISA.
  · Paired baseline and Week 24 samples were analyzed in 19 patients.

◆ 주요 결과 — Results
  · At Week 24, 38.2% of patients achieved SALT20 and 54.5% achieved SALT50; by Week 36, these rates increased to 49.3% and 60.3%, respectively.
  · Week 24 achievement of SALT20 or SALT50 was associated with shorter disease duration, lower baseline SALT score, and lower frequencies of AU/AT and eyebrow/eyelash involvement.
  · Compared with healthy controls, patients with AA showed distinct baseline plasma proteomic alterations.
  · Achievers showed a relatively higher baseline inflammatory plasma proteomic profile, and exploratory longitudinal analyses revealed broader post-treatment reductions in inflammatory proteins.
  · CCL11 was higher at baseline in patients who subsequently achieved SALT20 or SALT50 and remained associated with both endpoints in multivariable analysis.

◆ 결론 — Conclusions
  · Baricitinib response was heterogeneous in patients with severe AA.
  · Better outcomes were associated with higher baseline levels of several inflammatory plasma proteins.
  · CCL11 emerged as a candidate response-associated biomarker.
